findings.description: The duplicate-rows finding in openQuestions.md ends with a false claim about the data: it says the backfill attributes both copies of the four rows to `kendrick/skills#32`, but only the #27 archive's copies carry a `job` key at all — the #32 archive's four rows carry none, and by the file's own rule that makes them unattributed, not attributed to #32.
findings.evidence: _working-memory/openQuestions.md:37 reads "The backfill attributes both copies to `kendrick/skills#32` rather than deleting either". Derived from the data: `grep -c '"job"' ~/repos/skills/.agent-guild/state/archive/2026-08-08-issue-32/log/vendor-calls.jsonl` -> `0`, while `sed -n '8,11p' .../2026-08-08-issue-27/log/vendor-calls.jsonl | grep -o '"job": "[^"]*"'` -> four lines of `"job": "kendrick/skills#32"`. Python diff of the two archives, per row: `B 0 -> A 7 differing keys: {'job': ('kendrick/skills#32', None)}` and the same for B1->A8, B2->A9, B3->A10. The sentence also contradicts the one immediately before it (line 37), which correctly scopes the added key to "the #27 copies".

findings.description: The two counted findings are exactly right against the file: ten rows carry `/Users/karnett/` paths at precisely the indices named, and index 2 is the sole fractional-seconds `started_at`.
findings.evidence: `grep -c '/Users/karnett/' .../2026-08-08-issue-27/log/vendor-calls.jsonl` -> `10`; 0-based indices of those rows -> `1,3,4,6,8,12,13,14,15,16`, matching _working-memory/openQuestions.md:35 verbatim. Per-row `started_at` dump: index 2 = `2026-08-08T00:15:45.686223Z`, all 17 others whole-second (e.g. index 1 `2026-08-07T23:55:55Z`), matching openQuestions.md:36. Row count 18 confirmed by `wc -l` -> 18.

findings.description: The core of the third finding is accurate and correctly supersedes the constitution's now-stale "byte-identically" wording: indices 7-10 are the entire contents of the #32 archive, identical apart from the `job` key the backfill added.
findings.evidence: _working-memory/openQuestions.md:37 first sentence. Derived: #32 archive has 4 rows (`wc -l` -> 4); byte-identical rows shared with the #27 archive -> `[]`; rows matching once `job` is stripped -> `[0, 1, 2, 3]`, mapping to A indices 7, 8, 9, 10.

findings.description: The schema's `job` description says what the field holds, names the three-step derivation, and states that an absent key means unattributed with no null spelling.
findings.evidence: .agent-guild/schemas/vendor-call.schema.json:60-63 — "The guild run this call belongs to, written as that run's provenance ref (e.g. \"kendrick/skills#17\"). ledger-append.py takes it from --job, else from spec.md's provenance header, else leaves the key out. An absent key means the row is unattributed; that absence is the only spelling of it, since the field is never written as null." Confirmed optional in fact, not just in prose: properties 14, required 13, optional -> ['job'].

findings.description: ledger-append.py's module docstring documents the three-step precedence as a numbered list, and it matches what the code actually does.
findings.evidence: .agent-guild/scripts/ledger-append.py:21-33 — "1. `--job VALUE`, when passed. 2. Otherwise, the `ref` field from `.agent-guild/state/spec.md`'s provenance header, read from the current working directory ... 3. Otherwise, the `job` key is left out of the line entirely". Code agrees at line 214: `job = args.job if args.job is not None else derive_job()` followed by `if job is not None: line["job"] = job`.

findings.description: docs/vendor-ledger.md documents the field, its optionality, its three-step derivation, and the unattributed-not-null reading, in the register of the surrounding field list.
findings.evidence: docs/vendor-ledger.md:22 (field entry, "The one key in the line that can be absent"), :26 ("a row that doesn't is unattributed rather than attributed to nothing ... `properties` and deliberately not into `required`"), :28 (three steps, plus why `spec.md` resolves against the working directory), :33 (sample line carries `"job": "kendrick/skills#17"`), :54 (`--job VALUE` flag documented).

findings.description: dataContracts.md carries `job` in its Vendor Call Ledger description, and conventions.md carries the rule that a run's archive includes `log/`.
findings.evidence: _working-memory/dataContracts.md:65 — "`job` names the run a row came from ... It's the line's only optional key ... resolves it in three steps and no others". _working-memory/conventions.md:25-26 — "A run's archive holds everything under `.agent-guild/state/` that the run produced, `log/` among them ... The vendor ledger belongs to the record it documents, not to the directory the next job inherits." The supporting count checks out: 7 rows in the #27 archive carry `job: kendrick/skills#17`, matching "Seven crossings the #17 run made".

findings.description: The worker stayed in its lane: the retrospective SKILL.md edit predates every T-006 write, decisionLog.md and antipatterns.md are untouched, and activeContext.md is unmodified at 19 lines.
findings.evidence: `git status --porcelain` lists neither _working-memory/decisionLog.md, _working-memory/antipatterns.md, nor _working-memory/activeContext.md; `wc -l _working-memory/activeContext.md` -> 19. guild-core/workflows/retrospective/SKILL.md is modified but mtime 2026-08-10 19:58:40, versus 20:27:59-20:31:32 for the five files T-006 wrote, and its diff adds the archive-step content T-005 owns.
